tasks.title: Real Firefox Developer Edition user acceptance
tasks.acceptance: Exact candidate loaded in real browser and user confirms speech, quit, settings and no focus theft
partialEvidence: User confirmed Firefox Dev Edition temporary addon launches HUD, Preferences page displays, and actual installed Amy voice audibly speaks; also reported unexpected initial pause, single-sentence stall, and intermittent 1.9x+ popping on earlier candidates.

Fix candidate 96ec1aa: content-site autoplay NotAllowed falls back automatically to extension-owned player; subsequent sentences stay on same transport. CI uses Firefox normal autoplay policy instead of silently disabling it.

Real Firefox QA verified >=2 consecutive WAVs, nonzero reader boundaries, and Stop/Quit/reopen with no overlapping HTMLAudioElements; post-decoder 32ms high-rate volume attack and preserved audio element have synthetic regression tests.
Pending: user's live listening confirmation that 96ec1aa fixes initial start, entire text progression and 1.9x popping, plus focus and final acceptance.

2026-10-27 user confirmed 2x sentence starts laggy and word highlight trails after previous high-speed mitigation. Candidate e68a435 fixes dropped first-word boundary and decreases high-speed polling 50→16ms, tested in Gecko; no real acoustic confirmation.

2026-10-27 user independently confirmed pronunciation test bench at 2x has no onset pops, whereas full reader pops regardless of 0ms vs 1200ms sentence pause; preserve-pitch on/off sounded identical. Distinct pipelines identified: reader uses four abrupt 8ms gain steps and 48ms high-speed native fade vs clean bench's flat volume and 12ms native fade.

Candidate e8c54ad removes the reader's gain-stepping timer, uses full desired output gain immediately and restores 12ms native PCM fade at all rates. All three CI jobs green (40618114069); physical auditory improvement still unverified.

2026-10-28 user again reports audible popping at >=1.8x, while below 1.8x sounds clear. No assertion of acoustic fix. This threshold changes coalescing and highlight polling; full-reader background audio previously reused one media element while clean pronunciation bench created a new one per WAV.

3f2b8ad: new background Audio per WAV, strictly stop old before next; native/audio unit and disposable Firefox integration all green in run 40756503104. Await live candidate listening; potential coalescing path remains unproven.
2026-10-28 user explicitly confirmed 3f2b8ad still pops at 1.8x+ and reports intermittent repeated sentences; real Firefox audio acceptance remains FAILED, not complete.

Candidate f344ac2 (after aa0b43a / 000c0faa): page-owned reader now also uses a fresh media element per WAV, production disables >=1.8x cross-sentence coalescing, chunk completion is idempotent, and background playback provides 0.25s source-clock updates for stall detection. Synthetic engine probes passed; CI and audible user verification are pending.
2026-10-28 user confirms revision 19 improved but intermittently still hiccups near 1.8x, particularly on click-to-seek; audible acceptance remains open.

Revision 20 candidate: click-to-seek now ramps page-owned or background-owned live media volume to silence over 24ms before the existing authoritative cancel. Concurrent seek gestures only let the latest proceed; the old stop/release safety model is preserved. Isolated JS runtime mocks checked both audio fades and click ordering; full CI and live listening remain unverified.
2026-10-28 user reports revision 20 still pops/hiccups most of the time at 1.8x; repeatedly clicking the same word reproduces it. User listening gate remains FAILED.

Revision 21 candidate reuses byte-identical, bounded in-memory WAV data for matching voice/text/rate/pronunciation revision; unlike pronunciation test bench, prior reader requested fresh stochastic Piper synthesis every click. Pure JS production-path cache exercises and syntax checks passed, but actual real Piper audio and Firefox speaker playback have not been verified. A variable pop on identical cached WAVs implicates playback; a reproducible bad WAV implicates source synthesis.
2026-10-28 user reports revision 21 significantly reduces but does not eliminate intermittent 1.8x same-word playback pops. Acceptance is still FAILED.

Revision 22 candidate: native Python inserts 96 ms of actual zero PCM before speech for >=1.8x Gecko pitch processor startup, and reports startupPrerollMs. Reader subtracts preroll from speech-duration approximations then shifts all word timestamps by the preroll; same adjustment on cached replay. Regression tests added for native WAV bytes/duration/grouped offsets and JS cache alignment. User needs to reinstall the Firefox native host because installer copies the Python source. Synthetic JS method exercise passed; real speaker acceptance and full CI unverified.

2026-10-28 user reports revision 22 caused more frequent audible high-rate pops; 96ms startup pre-roll FAILED real listening and is fully reverted in revision 23. Previously implemented deterministic WAV caching and click-fade are retained; high-rate audio still NOT ACCEPTED.

2026-10-28 comparison with pinned sguzman/edge-tts development/linux-piper-v1 confirms both normal reader paths use HTMLAudioElement playbackRate and preservesPitch; Chromium/Gecko differ in media processing. Next candidate should avoid an endless series of speculative Gecko media ramps: first isolate or bypass browser time stretch, with actual acoustic verification before promotion.

lastGreenCI.note: All 3 jobs green after new Audio element per distinct Piper WAV in extension background rather than repeated source reload into a shared element. Unit regression checks 1.7x, 1.8x, 2.0x, verifies prior element stopped/source released/no overlap. No direct physical speaker evidence; user reports pops in prior candidate.

blockers.detail: Actual authenticated ChatGPT Writing Block extraction and typing focus behavior remain unverified by live user acceptance. Isolated Gecko synthetic fixture passes.

Failed live acceptance: 1.8x pop still intermittent and revision 22 96ms pre-roll reportedly increased frequency. Pre-roll and word offset modifications reverted in revision 23; repo restored to functional code of revision 21, not yet acoustically accepted. Future solution requires controlled browser processing isolation (e.g. offline tempo processing then Firefox playbackRate=1), not unverified fades. No real speaker evidence of success.
